source_text:
2.8 Πρὸς <τὸ> πληγήν
τινα ἄνευ ῥαφῆς κολλῆσαι Ἐπείπερ ἐν πολέμῳ πολλάκις τινὲς τιτρωσκόμενοι, τῆς
ἐκ σιδήρου διαιρέσεως μεγάλης οὔσης, ῥαφαῖς τὸ μᾶλλον δαμάζονται, πρὸς τοῦτο
φυσικὸν ἐφεύρομεν βοήθημα, τὸ ἄνευ ῥαφῆς κολλῆσαι δυνάμενον· ἔστι δὲ τοῦτο· βολβὸν ὃν ἐσθίομεν λειώσας ἐπιτίθει, καὶ παρακολλήσει.
pass_a_gloss: 2.8 Toward the a-wound some without suture to-glue. Since in war often some being-wounded, of-the from-iron division being great, by-sutures the more they-are-subdued, toward this a natural help we-found, the without suture to-glue being-able; is but this: a bulb which we-eat having-pounded set-on, and it-will-glue-beside.
pass_b_english: To glue a wound without a suture. Since in war some, being wounded, the division from iron being great, are the more subdued by sutures, toward this we found a natural help able to glue without a suture. It is this: pound the bulb which we eat, set it on, and it will glue beside.

choices.english: are the more subdued by sutures
choices.why: The iron cut is bad; the sewing subdues the wounded still more. Not 'they tame sutures'.

anf_compare.notes: No PD English of the Cesti body; ANF has the letters only.
